old_title: Iran war live: Blow to peace as crucial talks postponed after Trump's wild claim
new_title: Iran war live: US facing weapons shortages after dozens of aircraft destroyed
old_text:
Oman announced late on Sunday that planned talks with Iran about the future of the Strait of Hormuz had been cancelled "in the interests of consensus", scuppering hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough in the near term.
Foreign minister Sayyid Badr Albusaidi said the meeting had been postponed, without a clear alternative date set. He said Oman remained committed to "fostering dialogue that supports stability and lasting cooperation in our region".
Iranian officials had said earlier that they would attend the gathering with Gulf Arab states to present an agreement with Oman on the future governing of shipping routes through the Strait, which carried about a fifth of global oil supplies before the war.
The international waterway was free to cross before the war and shipping companies have warned such an agreement could set a dangerous precedent. Formal control of the Strait of Hormuz would also hand Iran more leverage in future talks with the US.
The channel continued to pose risks for oil shipping as it was reported on Sunday that a vessel had been struck by a projectile during transit, causing a fire and forcing the crew to evacuate. Oil prices surged to $102.35 on Monday morning.
Missile attacks target Iranian Kurdish opposition camps
Missile attacks targeted three camps belonging to Iranian Kurdish opposition groups east of Sulaimaniya in Iraq's Kurdistan region early on Monday, two security sources told Reuters, adding that no casualties were reported.
US pilot survived for two days behind enemy lines with broken back after Iran shot down plane: 'It was terrifying'
The American air force colonel whose fighter jet was downed over Iran in April has shared how survived for two days behind enemy lines with a broken back, arm and shoulder while waiting for help to arrive.
'Bravo' was the weapons-system officer in a two-man crew flying over Iran on 3 April when their F-15E Strike Eagle was hit by Iranian fire. The pilot in the front - 'Alpha' - ejected successfully, but Bravo came down in the mountains.
In his first public account of what happened, he told CBS News' 60 Minutes how he free-fell to the ground at speeds of up to 100mph with a damaged parachute, torn up by an Iranian shoulder-fired missile.

Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen claim new attacks on Saudi Arabia
Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen claimed new attacks on neighboring Saudi Arabia over the weekend, as Yemen's Saudi-backed government acknowledged the rebels' swift advance along the Red Sea coast as a "painful" development in a new front in the Iran war.
The Houthis' capture of a key port city and an island on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a crucial shipping alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, in recent days has alarmed markets and Yemeni civilians who fear a return to devastating civil war.
Overnight into Sunday, the Houthis claimed more attacks with missiles and drones on Saudi Arabia, which supports Yemen's internationally recognized government that's been fighting the rebels.
A Houthi military spokesperson, Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree, claimed in a statement that they targeted a military base in Sharurah province in Saudi Arabia's Najran region. He didn't provide evidence or say when the attack occurred.
He said the group had targeted "weapons depots and command and control centers" with ballistic missiles and drones.
The escalation follows a lightning Houthi advance to the Red Sea coast this week, giving the group greater power to attack Saudi ships around the Bab-al Mandeb strait.
Catch up: Trump says he could keep Iranian oil 'like Venezuela' as Hormuz talks face setback
US president Donald Trump has suggested his forces could stay in Iran and "keep the oil", drawing a parallel with a US push to take control of a fifth of Venezuela's vast oil reserves.
Trump reiterated that he still expected the Iran war to end this year even as the gridlock over talks on the Strait of Hormuz continue. Trump added that the price of gasoline would "drop like a rock" once the Iran war ended.
On Monday crude oil spiked to $107 a barrel, one of the highest since the US and Israel launched its war on Iran.Trump said that he would only make the "right deal", before drawing a parallel with the US deal in Venezuela, announced in August.
"We'll ultimately get out (of Iran), unless we decide to stay and keep the oil like Venezuela," Trump said, adding that the US revenue from Venezuela has "paid for the war many times".
Meanwhile, Oman said it had to postpone a meeting scheduled for Monday in Muscat with Iran and other regional countries to discuss the Strait of Hormuz "in the interest of consensus".
Saudi crown prince MBS meets with US Centcom chief
Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman has met the commander of US Central Command, Admiral Brad Cooper, state TV reports.
The pair met previously this time last month and discussed defence cooperation between the two countries as well as efforts to reduce regional tensions.
The latest visit comes amid questions over US support for its ally Saudi Arabia as the Iran-aligned Houthi rebels ramp up their attacks on the kingdom and push towards the coast, threatening Saudi shipping.
Saudi Arabia is the largest exporter of crude oil in the world.
US Air Force officer shot down in Iran recounts his two-day wait for help with a broken back
The American air force colonel whose F-15E fighter jet was downed over Iran in April has shared how survived for two days behind enemy lines with a broken back, arm and shoulder while waiting for help to arrive.
'Bravo' was the weapons-system officer in a two-man crew flying over Iran on 3 April, 2026 when the plane was hit by Iranian fire. The pilot in the front - 'Alpha' - ejected successfully, but Bravo went down in the mountains.
In his first public account of what happened, he told CBS News how he free-fell to the ground at speeds of up to 100mph with a damaged parachute, torn up by an Iranian shoulder-fired missile.
The officer broke his back, an arm and his shoulder after hitting the ground at speed, CBS reported. He said it was a "modern day miracle" that he survived two days hiding out before his rescue.
Finding himself in a valley with cliffs on either side, the officer concluded he would be safest in the high ground and climbed to a 7,000ft ridgeline despite his injuries.
"Never let a lack of motivation put you on Iranian TV," he said.
South Korea condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
South Korea's foreign ministry on Monday condemned what it said was a Houthi attack on civilian and economic facilities in southern Saudi Arabia that injured multiple civilians, and urged the Iran-aligned group to immediately stop such attacks.
The ministry said in a statement that attacks on civilians, civilian facilities and actions that undermined free and safe navigation could not be justified under any circumstances, and expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia.
Houthis claim attack on another Saudi airbase
Yemen's Houthis have claimed an attack on Saudi Arabia's Khamis Mushait air base.

Oman says talks with Iran have been postponed
Oman says that a planned meeting with Iran and regional Gulf states about the future of the Strait of Hormuz has been postponed in the "interests of consensus".
"It has been decided to postpone to a later date the regional meeting that was to be held on Monday in Salalah, in order to create conditions conducive to a constructive dialogue," the Oman News Agency said.
Iranian officials had said they would attend that gathering with Gulf Arab states to present an agreement with Oman on governing shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of global oil supplies before the war.
new_text:
The US military is facing a weapons shortage after dozens of aircraft have been destroyed in its war on Iran, the Pentagon has said, as the cost of the war hit $33.4 billion (£24.8bn).
In a report to Congress on Monday, the Defense Department's inspector general noted the destruction of four F-15 fighter jets and as many as 30 MQ-9 Reaper drones, and damage to one F-35 jet and seven KC-135 tanker aircraft.
It also said that Iranian attacks had "damaged and destroyed hundreds of buildings and structures at US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Oman, and Jordan during the conflict".
Some $22.3bn of cost is down to expended munitions, the report said.
Between 28 February and 30 June, Operation Epic Fury has caused "strategic inventory shortfalls and revealed industrial base bottlenecks for munitions resupply".
It comes as President Donald Trump has said he is "open" to negotiations to end the war with Iran, but stressed the final decision rests with him.
Saudi authorities warn of danger in Mecca amid Houthi escalation
Saudi authorities have warned of a potential danger in Mecca, home to Islam's holiest site, amid an escalation with Yemen's Houthis.
Minutes later, Saudi civil defence said the danger had cleared.
The brief alerts had also covered the provinces of Taif and Jeddah, state TV reported.
The Iran-aligned Houthis have launched a new wave of attacks on Saudi Arabia and are seizing positions on the western coast of Yemen along the Red Sea, Yemeni officials said, with discussions ongoing in Riyadh over how to respond to their lightning advance.
Vessel struck in Strait of Hormuz, says UKMTO
A vessel has been hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, a verified source has told the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).
No damage or environmental impact was reported after the Tuesday strike, the UKMTO said, and authorities are investigating.
We'll bring you more as it comes in.
UN Security Council to hold meeting over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait
The UN Security Council will hold a meeting on Tuesday to discuss the situation in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, two French diplomats have told the Reuters news agency.
The meeting, which was called by France, will be held on Tuesday afternoon, New York time, they said.
Full report: US watchdog tallies Iran war's hit to weapons stockpiles, military bases and more
A U.S. government watchdog released its first report on the impact of the Iran war on Monday, acknowledging the military's advanced weapons shortfalls and offering the first public look at the damage to American aircraft, bases and diplomatic outposts in the Middle East.
Much of the information has been previously reported over the past six months, but the Pentagon inspector general's report offered the fullest official accounting so far of the conflict's costs in American lives, taxpayer dollars and physical damage. It included information from the watchdogs for the Defense and State departments as well as the U.S. Agency for International Development.

Iranian foreign minister to meet Chinese counterpart in Beijing
Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi is set to visit China on 16 September, the foreign ministry in Beijing has said.
Araghchi will meet with Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi.
The pair met in Kyrgyzstan in late July, where they discussed the situation in the Middle East, described in a statement by the Chinese mission to the UN as a "matter of deep concern to China".
Trump: Countries must reimburse us for securing Strait of Hormuz
Donald Trump has demanded that the "Countries of the World" pay the US for its military action to secure the Strait of Hormuz.
"The Countries of the World, which have been no help to us whatsoever, should, and will, reimburse the United States of America when this SCAM Confligration is all over," he wrote in a post on Truth Social.
The US president was repeating his claim that Tehran "wants to make a deal, quickly and badly".
He added: "I will determine whether or not the U.S.A. will choose to engage - The concept of which we are open to."

US facing weapons shortages after dozens of aircraft destroyed - as cost of war hits $33bn
The US military is facing weapons shortages as a result of its war on Iran, the Defense Department's inspector general has said, after dozens of aircraft were destroyed in the region.
In a report to Congress on Monday, the inspector estimated that the US war on Iran has cost Washington $33.4 billion (£24.8 bn), most of which was spent on expended munitions.
The US military has lost dozens of aircraft, including the destruction of four F-15 fighter jets and as many as 30 MQ-9 Reaper drones, and damage to one F-35 jet and seven KC-135 tanker aircraft.
"Iranian strikes damaged and destroyed hundreds of buildings and structures at US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Oman, and Jordan during the conflict," the report says, without confirming what the cost was of the damage to these buildings.
Between 28 February and 30 June, Operation Epic Fury has caused "strategic inventory shortfalls and revealed industrial base bottlenecks for munitions resupply".
Saudi crown prince to meet Egypt's leader
Egypt's president Abdel Fattah al-Sisi is set to roll out the red carpet for Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman on Tuesday, the Egyptian presidency said.
The meeting comes against the backdrop of intensified fighting between Iranian-backed Houthi rebels and Yemen's Saudi-backed government.
The two leaders will hold a bilateral meeting to discuss the Houthi offensive and developments in Iran.
The Houthi rebels' weeklong offensive has culminated in the capture of Yemen's Red Sea coast, cementing their hold on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, through which Saudi oil transits.
Earlier, Cairo rejected a proposal from the Houthis for direct talks to coordinate maritime traffic through the waterway and the Red Sea, according to Qatari media outlet Al-Araby Al-Jadeed.
US imposes fresh sanctions on Russia's VTB Bank over alleged Iran ties
The United States imposed new sanctions on Russia's VTB Bank on Monday, accusing the lender of helping Iran evade Western sanctions and warning that foreign institutions that continue doing business with Russia's second-largest bank could face additional penalties.
Already cut off from the dollar system over Russia's invasion of Ukraine, VTB now faces Iran-related sanctions that Treasury officials said could expose foreign banks and businesses that continue to deal with it to additional penalties.
Treasury said VTB had opened offices in Iran, established banking relationships with sanctioned Iranian lenders and helped build financial channels designed to facilitate trade and financial coordination between Moscow and Tehran.
The action, taken under an executive order aimed at increasing pressure on the Iranian economy, adds to US sanctions already in place against VTB Bank that were imposed in February 2022.
The Treasury said in a statement that state-controlled VTB was now "among the most comprehensively sanctioned financial institutions in the world." The Iran-related penalties would increase the risk of secondary sanctions against foreign institutions that continue to do business with VTB, the Treasury added.
"Under Operation Economic Outcast, Treasury will continue to target and disrupt those who provide material, technological, or financial support that allows the Iranian regime to sustain its terrorist enterprise," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in the statement.
"Treasury will not tolerate any support to the regime and will continue to identify, expose, and isolate Iran's enablers," it quoted him as saying.
